recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. A future terminology cleanup may separately audit unused duplicate value set files under resource folders, especially source/medicationrequest/valueset-administration-method-codes.xml, but that stale copy is outside this active-source correction.
issue_request: FHIR-19913 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for Pharmacy. It asked to review the Dosage.method value set so administration-method examples such as infusion, IV bolus, and IV push could be supported; the accepted resolution changed the binding basis from SNOMED CT 422096002 Dosing instruction fragment to 736665006 Dose form administration method and said to fix the long-description examples.
initial_application: Historical commit 1dcdc4c567 changed the active source/datatypes/valueset-administration-method-codes.xml filter from 422096002 to 736665006, and current release-history output also shows R5 using 736665006. The example wording was not applied: active Dosage.method still said "Slow Push; Deep IV," and active MedicationAdministration.dosage.method retained the same stale examples. A source/medicationrequest copy still contains 422096002, but source references and fhir.ini do not identify it as the current binding source.
additional_context: Pharmacy Confluence minutes record the FHIR-19913 disposition as changing the binding to administration method and fixing examples in the description, with an 8-0-0 Persuasive with Modification vote. The referenced Zulip Mapping infusion discussion explains the route/method distinction and supports avoiding examples that combine intravenous route with administration method.
reconciliation: Changed the active Dosage.method requirements text and the parallel active MedicationAdministration.dosage.method definition from "Slow Push; Deep IV" to "inject, swallow, or chew." The active value set filter remained 736665006.
source_changes: source/datatypes/dosage.xml: updated Dosage.method examples to "inject, swallow, or chew."
source/medicationadministration/structuredefinition-MedicationAdministration.xml: updated MedicationAdministration.dosage.method examples to match the administration-method guidance.
